summary: Two findings: one medium, one low. (1) The map's four alreadyRecorded links, AlgebraicCurves Layers 7, 8, 9 and 12 → ModularCurves Layer 10, are not recorded anywhere. This map defers them to the ModularCurves link map, and that map's review removed the same four as 'Already in AlgebraicCurves packet'. The two reviews merged seven seconds apart on 23 September. The production graph (2840 stages, 8007 edges) therefore has no AlgebraicCurves → ModularCurves edge at all, although ModularCurves Layer 10 names these four layers as the suppliers of its Hurwitz/different package. (2) Two examined entries (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups, KTheoryLowDegrees) say 'no AlgebraicCurves output', which accepted restructurings RS-29 and RS-18 contradict. Their edges are live through data/restructure, so this affects only the record. Everything else tested holds: all 46 links and 11 overlaps have literal quotes on existing endpoints, the link directions and the independent review's boundaries are sound, and a catalogue-wide vocabulary screen found no further missing consumer.

Library claim in link 4's review boundary ('Point.toClass_surjective is already proved at the pin, with no ellipticity assumption'): true at Tau Ceti f790474, TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Point/ToClass.lean:655, over any affine Weierstrass curve with [DecidableEq F]. Mathlib 082e2d3 has Point.toClass (Affine/Point.lean:752) but not the surjectivity.

Negative decisions tested against the texts. ComplexComparisonPartII C4: Layer 12C proves essential surjectivity for projective models, but no layer states the open embedding of an affine curve, so there is no exact match. JacobianChallenge Layer E: 'dim Jac X = genus X' uses JacobianChallenge's own g := dim H¹(X, 𝒪_X) (Layer B), so the AlgebraicCurves document's claim that it consumes this roadmap's genus is not supported by the consumer's text. SchemeKTheoryOperations S.7 and KU-geometry: general GRR and a pseudo-supplier for vector bundles, neither an output of these layers. EllipticKTheory E.7: its supplier is ambiguous, as the map says.

Catalogue-wide screen of all 2840 stages not already joined to AlgebraicCurves, for Riemann–Roch, Riemann–Hurwitz, Hurwitz formula or bound, Weil differential, repartition, Goppa or AG codes, hyperelliptic, plane curve, Weierstrass points, Clifford, canonical divisor or class, constant field, places, Kähler differential, different, Artin–Schreier, Kummer covers, Tsen, Carlitz, Drinfeld, k(x) and F_q(t). Every hit was read in context. They are analytic or topological Riemann–Hurwitz (BelyiMaps L0/L8, ModularForms L10, FuchsianOrbifolds), Tate's adelic RR (AN.4), coherent H¹-vanishing on modular curves (AlgebraicModularForms R15.2, whose owner is JacobianChallenge Layer B), Clifford algebras, Drinfeld level structures, curves supplied through FunctionFieldArithmetic or SF.3, or example-only uses (FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.7's hyperelliptic acceptance case). None is a missing direct dependency of this map.

Accepted restructurings naming AlgebraicCurves: RS-18 (links from Layer 12 to EllipticKTheory E.1–E.3, KU-curvek, EllipticRegulators ER.1, KTheoryLowDegrees Z.5–Z.6 and SchemeKTheoryOperations KU-geometry and KU-operations) and RS-29 (Layer 8 → InverseGalois IG.1) are all live. RS-04 (not accepted) narrows FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.0–FA.3 and FA.7 onto AlgebraicCurves, consistent with this map's overlaps 5–7.

Duplication: overlaps 0–10 re-read. The Tau Ceti–Tau Ceti overlaps are 'keep', as §15 requires. The FunctionFieldArithmetic rescopes match RS-04's owners table. No other proposed roadmap plans function-field places, divisors or Riemann–Roch outside these recorded overlaps.
Cycle test: inserting the four missing AlgebraicCurves → ModularCurves Layer 10 edges into the production edge set gives 8011 edges and no directed cycle.

findings.claim: Four dependencies, AlgebraicCurves Layers 7, 8, 9 and 12 → ModularCurves Layer 10, are recorded by neither map, because each map's review deduplicated them against the other. This map moved them to alreadyRecorded with recordedIn research/blueprint/links/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_ModularCurves.json. That map's review removed exactly these four pairs with the reason 'Already in AlgebraicCurves packet.' Neither the research copies nor the promoted copies in data/links carry them. The production graph has no edge from any AlgebraicCurves layer into ModularCurves, so the atlas shows ModularCurves Layer 10 as independent of the roadmap it names as supplier of its Hurwitz/different package.
findings.evidence: ModularCurves Layer 10 (data/atlas.json) says the Hurwitz/different computation is 'a named dependency package, not a footnote, and one whose supplier now exists: the [Algebraic Curves roadmap](../AlgebraicCurves/README.md) owns the different divisor, Dedekind's different theorem, and the Hurwitz genus formula (its Layer 7), … Hilbert's different formula … (its Layer 8 …), and the Kähler-differential comparison (its Layer 9); its Layer 12 dictionary carries those function-field statements to the smooth proper fibres used here'. This map's alreadyRecorded entries have the reason 'Valid … input; deduplicate against the ModularCurves packet.' The ModularCurves map's review.removed has these four pairs, each with the reason 'Already in AlgebraicCurves packet.' The two reviews merged within seconds of each other: c9da9073 at 2026-09-23 16:28:55 UTC (this map) and 12bb58b6 at 16:29:02 UTC (ModularCurves). scripts.build.assemble(require_distances=False) at 2bfd3bd2 gives 2840 stages and 8007 edges; none of the four pairs is present, and no edge runs from an AlgebraicCurves stage to a ModularCurves stage. Adding the four pairs in memory gives 8011 edges and no directed cycle.
findings.fix: Record the four pairs once, as links of this (focal) map, not of the ModularCurves map, whose review removed them. Move AC-L28–AC-L31 from alreadyRecorded into links, keeping their recorded evidence, with confidence 'inferred': the consumer names the supplier's layers, but the AlgebraicCurves document does not name ModularCurves. Keep AC-L31's boundary: relative constancy of χ is not supplied. Correct the summary and the review note that describes them as recorded elsewhere, and leave the ModularCurves map unchanged. The corrected packet needs a renewed independent review so that promote.py copies it into data/links. Afterwards, check with the assembler that the four edges are live.

findings.claim: Two examined records say the neighbour uses no AlgebraicCurves output, and accepted restructurings contradict both. InverseGalois: 'Étale π₁, Riemann existence (ComplexComparisonPartII) and Hurwitz spaces; … No AlgebraicCurves output.' But accepted RS-29 makes Layer 8 the owner of 'Finite function-field decomposition/inertia groups and lower ramification theory' (formerly IG.1) and links Layer 8 → IG.1. KTheoryLowDegrees: 'Z.5 covers K₀ and Pic of regular curves at scheme level; no AlgebraicCurves output.' But accepted RS-18 narrows Z.5 with Layer 12 among its suppliers and links Layer 12 → Z.5 and → Z.6. The edges are live through data/restructure, so the graph is right, but the map's catalogue record is wrong and would mislead a later screen. The RS-18 contradiction already existed at review time, since RS-18 was promoted on 21 September. The RS-29 one arose later, when RS-29 was promoted on 23 September at 20:22 UTC.
